product.summary: A local-first toolkit that helps AI agents build and reuse an approved design system.
product.problem: Design decisions are frequently lost across agent sessions and collaborators, causing duplicated components and inconsistent interface rules.
product.valueProposition: Hatch gives agents one machine-readable source for approved design decisions and registered Figma components without requiring a hosted service.

goals.statement: Agents reuse the approved Button instead of drawing a visual approximation.
goals.successSignal: A page request resolves one registered component and inserts a real Figma Instance.

goals.statement: A contributor can run the first vertical slice on a local computer.
goals.successSignal: The Button demonstration completes without a project cloud server or database.

audiences.name: Product designer
audiences.description: A designer establishing the visual and component foundation for a new product.
needs: Keep final authority over visual direction and component approval.
Make approved decisions reusable by several agents and collaborators.

audiences.name: Agent-assisted builder
audiences.description: A contributor using Codex or another agent to create product interfaces.
needs: Find the correct component without relying on chat memory.
Receive a clear recovery action when no approved component exists.

scenarios.name: Create the initial component library
scenarios.description: The designer approves the foundation and asks an agent to build the registered Figma Button assets.

scenarios.name: Reuse an approved Button
scenarios.description: An agent queries the registry and inserts a real Button Instance into a product page.

principles: Make system status and human approval boundaries visible.
Prefer calm, precise communication over decorative complexity.
avoid: Do not imply that an unapproved generated component is production-ready.
Do not use visual novelty to hide unclear system behavior.

constraints.statement: The first release must work without a project cloud server, database, or account system.
Visual direction and production component decisions require explicit human approval.
All managed Figma writes must pass through one serialized Plugin writer.

requirements: Communicate important status with text or structure, not color alone.
Support keyboard operation for interactive Plugin controls.
Preserve readable contrast for enabled and disabled Button states.

references.name: Public design-system example
references.reason: Demonstrates how a public reference can explain intent without embedding a private Figma locator.
